tagline.text: An adventure park where you fling yourself out over the Wahig River canyon

children.text: A municipal adventure park set in the Wahig River canyon in the inland village of Danao, Bohol. From the Canyon Swing Plunge off a cliff edge to a zipline and cable car crossing the canyon, plus kayaking and cave exploring, it's all here — making for one of Bohol's most thrilling days out.

Danao Adventure Park sits in Barangay Magtangtang in the town of Danao, in the inland northeast of Bohol Island. Its official name is E.A.T. Danao, standing for Eco, Educational, and Extreme adventure tourism, and it's run directly by the Danao municipal government. Built around the Wahig River canyon, cut deep through limestone terrain, and the surrounding forest and caves, the park spans about 144 hectares and hosts a range of adventure facilities.
The park's signature attraction is the Canyon Swing Plunge (The Plunge), which has drawn attention since around

. Jumping off a cliff at the canyon's edge, you free-fall for a few seconds before swinging across the canyon like a giant pendulum — billed as one of the most extreme experiences in the Philippines. Also popular are the Suislide, a seated zipline that runs back and forth over the canyon, and the Sky Ride, a cable-car-style crossing of the gorge.
Danao also holds a special place in Philippine history. In
, the Boholano Francisco Dagohoy rose up against Spanish rule and based his resistance in these mountains — a rebellion that lasted about 85 years, until

, making it the longest-running uprising in Philippine history. Near the park stand a marker commemorating Dagohoy and a cave said to have sheltered him, so you can pick up a bit of history along with the adventure.

It suits travelers who've already seen Panglao's beaches and the Chocolate Hills and want something different, as well as groups of friends and active families. Each facility is priced separately, so you can pick and choose only what you want; and even if extreme activities aren't your thing, lighter options like kayaking, a walk to the viewpoint, or cave exploring still let you take in the canyon scenery fully.

blocks.title: Kayaking and Tubing on the Wahig River

children.text: Head down into the canyon floor to kayak or tube the calm Wahig River with a guide. Looking up at cliffs and forest rising on either side from the water is a distinctive experience.
The roughly
Camira Cave is a beginner-friendly route with stalactites, stalagmites, and underground pools. More challenging cave routes are also available, sometimes with a minimum group-size requirement.

Near the park stands a marker honoring Dagohoy, leader of the longest rebellion in Philippine history, along with the cave where he is said to have taken refuge. Ask at the park's information desk for directions.

Most visitors stay in Panglao or Tagbilaran and come for the day, but given the travel time, staying overnight inside the park or in downtown Danao makes for a much more relaxed visit. The park runs affordably priced rooms and group lodging around the canyon, so it's worth checking availability on the official page or by phone before you go. Around Panglao's Alona Beach, guesthouses run about
a night, and beach resorts about

Inside the park, a café serves Filipino home-style dishes, fried rice, sweet-and-sour pork, and drinks, enough for lunch. Danao is a quiet farming town with few restaurant options, so it's a good idea to bring snacks and water from Tagbilaran. On the way back, stopping in Carmen, home of the Chocolate Hills, or at the Loboc River lets you enjoy a buffet at a floating restaurant on a raft; Bohol specialties worth trying include the peanut candy peanut kisses and the glutinous-rice sweet calamay, served in a coconut shell.
Opening hours generally run from about
8 AM
to around
5 PM
, and activities often stop taking bookings before closing time, so arrive in the morning.
Fees are charged separately per attraction, and combo discount packages are available, so compare your options at the entrance. Rates were revised in
, so check the latest prices.
The Plunge and zipline have weight, age, and health requirements, so if you have a heart condition or back injury, talk to staff in advance.
Since you'll need to wear a harness, fitted pants and sneakers are more comfortable than shorts, and it's best to check your hat and sunglasses before the ride.
Kayaking, tubing, and cave exploring will get your clothes wet, so bring a change of clothes and a waterproof bag.
There are hardly any ATMs around the park, so bring plenty of cash.
If traveling by public transport, the last vans and buses back run early, so it's safest to leave the park before
3 PM
If you bring an action camera, staff can sometimes clip it to your harness, but be sure to secure it with a strap so it doesn't fall.

High-elevation activities like the Plunge and zipline are suspended in strong wind, rain, or lightning. Always follow staff safety briefings and instructions, and don't ride if any equipment looks questionable.
All extreme activities are off-limits after drinking alcohol, and pregnant travelers or anyone with high blood pressure or a heart condition should not participate.
Some spots along the canyon viewpoint and cliff edge lack railings, so don't get too close while taking photos.
After heavy rain, the Wahig River's water level can rise suddenly, so don't head down to the river without a guide.
The caves are slippery and dark, so wear a headlamp and helmet and stay with your guide at all times.
Fees, operating hours, and weight limits change often, so check the park's official page for the latest notices before visiting.
